newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Research institute says Hungary recovery uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Research institute says Hungary recovery uncertain.

text.p: An independent research institute on Wednesday said the timing of Hungary's economic recovery still remains uncertain.
"The beginning of the economic recovery is not certain," the institute, GKI, said in its monthly report published by the Hungarian economic news agency MTI-Econews.
The report predicted a slowdown in export growth and an acceleration in imports. As a result, this year's trade deficit will remain at the 1995 level of $2.6 billion, it said. @

The study reported a 7.5 percent fall in capital investments in the first three quarters compared to the same period of last year and described this as "the most remarkable economic statistic of the month."
The fall hit mainly infrastructure and non-productive sectors, GKI said, but forecast that the full-year figure would still match that of 1995.

Industrial output was up six percent in September over August, but GKI estimates a two percent increase in industrial production over the first eleven months and predicts a three percent increase for the whole of 1996. @

The current account deficit will be reduced to $1.7 billion this year from $2.5 billion in 1995, the study says, while government budget deficit is expected to end the year only slightly above the four-percent-of-GDP limit agreed with the International Monetary Fund in March.
GKI estimates the eleven-month consumer price inflation at 24 percent and a year-end figure of 23.7 percent, in line with a government forecast of 22-24 percent. @

In general the position of macroeconomic balances are favourable, the report said, with the level of external debt falling and no financing difficulties and forecast slow and gradual recovery for the future.
"Hungary's economic prospects could even be termed as promising if hopes for the beginning of economic growth prove to be realistic, but this is still uncertain," the GKI forecast concluded.
